headline: Secretagogues by day
punch: There is a study on why that fights itself.

headline: The plan sounds right
body: So the proposed design is secretagogues through the day to create pulses, and exogenous growth hormone at night to cover the big nocturnal window. Two tools, each doing the thing it is good at, covering different parts of the clock. | It is a reasonable-sounding plan and there is a human experiment that tested the interaction directly. The result is the opposite of additive, and the mechanism behind it is already familiar from the somatostatin post.

headline: Richmond 2002
body: Prepubertal boys, midpubertal boys and young men. Each subject underwent four randomly ordered infusion days: saline then saline, saline then GHRH, a pulse of **recombinant GH** then saline, and GH then GHRH. | The GH was given as a 6-minute square-wave intravenous pulse at 08:30. The GHRH challenge came at 10:30, two hours later. So the question is simple: does an earlier GH pulse change what a later stimulus can produce?
punch: A pulse of GH, then a GHRH challenge two hours on.

headline: What did the GH pulse do?
body: **Injection of rhGH attenuated subsequent GHRH-stimulated peak serum GH concentrations.** The earlier dose measurably blunted the later pulse, two hours downstream. | And the mechanism is named in the first line of the paper: a single injected pulse of GH inhibits later GH secretion through **central mechanisms that drive somatostatin and repress GHRH outflow**. So exogenous GH does not sit quietly next to your axis. It raises the brake on it.
punch: ==Exogenous GH raises the brake on your own pulses.==

headline: So the two halves
body: Follow the chain. Exogenous GH raises IGF-1, IGF-1 acts at the hypothalamus to raise somatostatin, somatostatin closes the gate, and the gate it closes is the exact one that both GHRH and GHRP have to pass through to do anything. | What this means is that you are paying for a secretagogue whose window you narrowed yourself a few hours earlier, with the other half of the same protocol.
punch: _The night dose taxes the next day's pulses._

headline: There is a real difference
body: The midpubertal boys showed greater fractional autoinhibition but also **markedly accentuated postnadir escape, a 4.6-fold steeper slope**, at P < 0.001 against both other groups. | So in midpuberty the axis climbs back out from under that feedback far faster than it does before puberty or in young adults. The suppression window is shorter rather than absent, which is a genuine and specific difference rather than a hand-wave about age.

headline: But where is your GH already?
body: Around **70%** of your daily GH already comes out in early sleep, during the window when somatostatin has naturally withdrawn and GHRH surges into the gap. That is the body's own largest pulse of the day, running without any help. | So placing exogenous GH there stacks it on top of the loudest hour you already have. Meanwhile the daytime trough, the part of the cycle that is genuinely empty, is the part this design leaves alone.
punch: ==The night dose lands where you are already loudest.==

headline: And the day half
body: Secretagogues run through the day hit two limits that are already measured. The ghrelin receptor fatigues within 24 hours of continuous exposure while the GHRH receptor does not fatigue in fourteen days. | And pyridostigmine, the cholinergic lever that would widen the window, enhanced the **first** GHRH pulse and **not the second**. So repeat dosing is not repeat benefit on either the receptor side or the gate side.
punch: Frequency is not the lever people think it is.

headline: What the evidence supports
body: Supported: GHRH plus a GHS is the most potent GH releaser known. Somatostatin gates both of them. Exogenous GH raises that gate for hours afterwards. The ghrelin arm fatigues and the GHRH arm does not. Four mechanisms, each measured. | Not supported: any specific schedule. Nobody has run the trial that compares these timings for growth in humans, and the one adjacent human trial tested dose splitting rather than pulsing.
punch: _Four mechanisms are solid. The schedule is not._

headline: What follows from mechanism
body: If exogenous GH suppresses the axis for hours afterwards, then it competes with any secretagogue placed near it in time, and it duplicates the pulse you already produce at sleep onset without help. | The arrangement that follows is spacing them so the GH is not sitting on the secretagogue window. That is reasoning from physiology, not a tested protocol, and it should be treated as exactly that and nothing more.
punch: ==This is an inference from physiology. Nobody has tested it.==

headline: The honest summary
body: Pattern beats dose. The brake decides what any accelerator is capable of. Local IGF-1 drives growth while serum IGF-1 fails to report it. And the one combination that has been tested directly turned out to be partly self-cancelling. | None of that tells you what to take. All of it tells you what to stop assuming, which is a less satisfying conclusion and a considerably more useful one.
punch: ==Stop optimising the number. Start asking what the gate is doing.==
